text:
maya: Heads up — since ~07:10 UTC we're seeing a spike of tiny GPU pods getting evicted in eu-west1, pods request 0.25-0.5 GPU and then bounce. Anyone watching scheduler logs?

jordan: Seeing that. eviction spikes + Pending -> Running -> Evicted loop. Autoscaler scaled down nodes and warm-pool reclaimed, then a ton of small jobs lost their place.

lee: Repro: workload with per-pod request ceiling=0.5 (the recent safety knob) + soft-affinity to nodetype:gpu-small. Scheduler seems to pack 1 tiny pod per GPU but then preempts them when a larger pod needs >0.5.

samir: Oof. We enabled that ceiling to avoid fractional overcommit, but didn't account for gang jobs that need >0.5. When a big job lands it preempts multiple small ones, causing cascading reschedules.

olivia: Logs show the scheduler's BestEffort binpacking heuristic picks small slots across racks, then the preemptor picks them off one-by-one. Net result: a lot of small pods starve and churn.

maya: ops-bot, can you dump a couple of sample scheduler traces and eviction reasons for a node?

ops-bot: Autoscaler event: scaledown 12 nodes in eu-west1 at 07:11:58 UTC.
ops-bot: Eviction summary (sample node n-gpu-23): 8 evicted pods in last 6m — reason: Preemption/InsufficientResources (gpu).

jordan: We also see NIC traffic spikes on those nodes during the churn (possible sidecars copying checkpoints?). Network saturation may amplify scheduling delays.

lee: I grabbed a scheduler trace:
```
E0821 07:12:05 scheduler.go:421 Pod "ml-train-9876" preempted pod "tiny-worker-55" on node n-gpu-23: required=1.0, victimRequests=[0.25 0.25 0.5]
```

samir: That trace nails it. Victim selection is scattered; preemptor removes several small pods but they all requeue and the binpacker keeps scattering them.

olivia: Cost side-effect: repeated pod restarts + partial GPU usage means higher billing with lower utilization. We should pause the ceiling rollout until we have a more deterministic placement.

maya: Agreed. Two quick mitigations: 1) Temporarily disable per-pod gpu-request-ceiling in eu-west1; 2) tighten soft-affinity to prefer packing into same GPU node for small pods (co-locate prefix-cached jobs).

jordan: Also propose a short-term admission controller tweak: batch-placement window (hold tiny pods for 10s and try to pack them as a gang) — reduces scattering.

lee: We can also change preemption policy to prefer evicting warm-pool placeholders or best-effort pods first, instead of tiny guaranteed pods.

samir: Is there telemetry? Can we surface 'tiny-pod churn rate' in Console so product teams see the impact?

olivia: I'll open an Optimize rule for a churn alert and attach a sample promptset that flags QoS regressions.

maya: I'll roll back the ceiling in eu-west1 to previous config now (15m cooldown). Leaving it enabled in other regions for safety.

ops-bot: Configuration change recorded: feature.per_pod_gpu_ceiling disabled in eu-west1 at 07:18:02 UTC by maya.

jordan: After rollback, eviction rate dropped by ~70% on the sampled nodes. Still seeing a few stragglers because of the reschedule backlog.

lee: Follow-ups: run a canary of the gang-placement admission change on a small dev pool; simulate large job arrivals and tiny-pod flood to validate.

samir: Also validate NIC egress patterns — add a sidecar backoff to checkpoint uploads for tiny-worker jobs.

olivia: I'll file the infra ticket and tag product owners for the ceiling policy (will include cost delta + churn graphs).

maya: Thanks all. If we see recurrence, we may need a more explicit fractional-GPU placement strategy (fractional packing per GPU with preemption groups). For now monitoring + rollback did the trick. :thumbsup:
